senses.def: the male ruler of a country that has a royal family
examples: The king addressed the nation on television after the earthquake.
She was crowned queen when the old king died.

senses.def: the most important or successful person or thing in a particular field
examples: He was known as the king of rock and roll.
In the jungle, the lion is often called the king of the animals.

note: "King-size" (extra large) is common for beds and products: a king-size bed.

senses.def: a country whose head of state is a king or queen
examples: The United Kingdom is made up of four countries.
The ancient kingdom stretched from the mountains to the sea.

senses.def: one of the main groups into which living things are divided
examples: Fungi were once classified as part of the plant kingdom.

senses.def: to touch someone with your lips to show love or to say hello or goodbye
examples: She kissed her son on the forehead before he left for school.
They kissed for the first time under the streetlight.

senses.def: an act of touching someone with your lips
examples: He gave his grandmother a kiss on the cheek.
She blew him a kiss from the train window.

senses.def: a set of tools or equipment kept together for a particular purpose
examples: Every car should carry a basic first-aid kit.
The plumber opened his tool kit and got to work.

senses.tr: (kendin monte et) parça seti, maket seti
senses.def: a set of parts that you put together yourself to make something
examples: My son spent the weekend building a model airplane from a kit.

note: In British English, "kit" also means sports clothes (football kit). Americans say "uniform" or "gear".

senses.def: the room where food is prepared and cooked
examples: We usually eat breakfast at the kitchen table.
The restaurant's kitchen was closed for a health inspection.

senses.def: the joint in the middle of your leg where it bends
examples: She hurt her knee while skiing and needed surgery.
The kids knelt on their knees to look under the bed.

note: The k is silent: /niː/. Related verb: kneel – knelt – knelt.

senses.def: a tool with a sharp metal blade and a handle, used for cutting or as a weapon
examples: Use a sharp knife to slice the tomatoes.
Police found the knife used in the attack.

note: Plural: knives. The k is silent: /naɪf/.

senses.def: to hit a door or window with your hand so that people inside know you are there
examples: Someone knocked on the door just after midnight.
Please knock before you come into my office.

senses.def: to hit something by accident so that it moves or falls
examples: The cat knocked a glass off the table.

senses.def: the sound of someone hitting a door to get attention
examples: There was a loud knock at the door.

note: Phrasal verbs: knock down (demolish), knock out (make unconscious), knock over (make fall).

senses.def: to have information in your mind because you learned it or were told it
examples: Do you know what time the store closes?
I didn't know that she had moved to Chicago.

senses.def: to be familiar with a person or place
examples: I've known him since we were in high school.
She knows the city really well.

note: Irregular: know – knew – known. Not used in continuous form: say "I know", not "I am knowing".

senses.def: the information, understanding and skills you get from education or experience
examples: She has a deep knowledge of Japanese history.
The job requires basic knowledge of accounting software.

senses.def: the state of knowing about a particular fact or situation
examples: The deal was made without my knowledge.
To my knowledge, nobody has complained yet.

note: Uncountable: say "a lot of knowledge", never "knowledges" or "a knowledge" (except "a good knowledge of").

senses.def: a laboratory; a room or building for scientific experiments and testing
examples: The blood samples were sent to the lab for testing.
Students spend two hours a week in the chemistry lab.

note: Informal short form of "laboratory", used far more often in everyday speech.

senses.def: a small piece of paper or material attached to something that gives information about it
examples: Always read the label before taking any medicine.
The price was printed on a label inside the jacket.

senses.def: a company that produces music recordings, or a brand of clothing
examples: The band signed with a major record label last year.

senses.def: to attach a label to something, or to describe someone in a way that is often unfair
examples: Make sure all the boxes are clearly labeled.
He was unfairly labeled a troublemaker at school.

note: American spelling: labeled, labeling. British: labelled, labelling.

senses.def: work, especially physical work, or the workers who do it
examples: The repair cost $200 for parts and $150 for labor.
Many farms depend on cheap seasonal labor.

senses.def: the process of giving birth to a baby
examples: She went into labor two weeks early.

note: British spelling: labour. "Labor Day" is a US holiday in September.

senses.def: a room or building where scientists do experiments, research or tests
examples: The vaccine was developed in a university laboratory.
Samples were analyzed in a government laboratory.

note: American stress is on the first syllable: LAB-ruh-tor-ee. British stress: la-BOR-uh-tree.

senses.def: the state of not having something or not having enough of it
examples: The project failed because of a lack of funding.
Lack of sleep can affect your concentration.

senses.def: to not have something, or not have enough of it
examples: He's talented but lacks confidence.
The report lacked any real detail.

note: The verb takes a direct object: "She lacks experience", not "lacks of experience". The noun uses "of".

senses.def: a boy or young man
examples: He was just a lad of sixteen when he joined the navy.
The old farmer hired a local lad to help with the harvest.

note: Mainly British and informal. Americans usually say "boy", "kid" or "guy".

senses.def: a piece of equipment with steps between two long sides, used for climbing up and down
examples: He climbed a ladder to clean the gutters.
Hold the ladder steady while I change the bulb.

senses.def: a series of levels in an organization or society that people try to move up
examples: She worked her way up the corporate ladder.

note: A ladder is portable. Fixed stairs in a building are "stairs" or "a staircase" — both are "merdiven" in Turkish.

senses.def: a polite word for a woman
examples: An elderly lady asked me for directions to the station.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats.

note: "The ladies' room" is a polite American term for a women's restroom. "First Lady" is the president's wife.

senses.def: a large area of water surrounded by land
examples: We rented a cabin by the lake for the summer.
In winter, the lake freezes over completely.

note: In names, "Lake" comes first and has no "the": Lake Van, Lake Superior.

senses.def: a device that produces light, especially one you can move around
examples: She switched on the lamp beside her bed and started reading.
The desk lamp was too dim to work by.

senses.def: the solid surface of the earth, or an area of ground owned by someone
examples: After three weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
They bought a piece of land to build a house on.

senses.def: a country or region (literary)
examples: Immigrants came to this land looking for a better life.

senses.def: to come down from the air onto the ground or another surface
examples: Our flight landed in Denver an hour late.
A bird landed on the windowsill.

senses.def: to succeed in getting something good, such as a job or contract (informal)
examples: She landed a job at a major tech company.

senses.def: the act of bringing an aircraft or spacecraft down to the ground
examples: The pilot made an emergency landing in a field.
The first moon landing took place in 1969.

senses.def: the flat area at the top of a set of stairs or between two sets of stairs
examples: The kids left their shoes on the landing outside the bedroom.

note: Opposite of "takeoff". A "landing page" is the first web page a visitor arrives at.

senses.def: a person or company that rents a house, apartment or office to someone
examples: Our landlord raised the rent by ten percent this year.
Call the landlord if the heating stops working.

note: Trap: Turkish "ev sahibi" also means "host". In English, landlord = the person you pay rent to; host = the person who invites guests.

senses.def: a building or place that is easy to see and recognize and helps you know where you are
examples: The Golden Gate Bridge is San Francisco's most famous landmark.
Turn left at the old church; it's a good landmark.

senses.def: an event, discovery or decision that marks an important stage or change
examples: The court's ruling was a landmark in civil rights history.
It was a landmark decision for gay rights.

note: "Landmark" is often used before a noun: a landmark ruling/case/study (= very important, historic).

senses.def: everything you can see when you look across a large area of land
examples: The desert landscape was flat and empty for miles.
Wind farms have changed the rural landscape.

senses.def: the general situation in a particular area of activity
examples: Streaming services have transformed the media landscape.

note: "Landscape" also means horizontal page orientation (opposite: portrait).

senses.def: one of the parts of a road marked for a single line of traffic
examples: The truck suddenly moved into the left lane.
Only buses can use this lane during rush hour.

senses.def: a narrow road, especially in the countryside
examples: We walked down a quiet country lane lined with trees.

note: "Life in the fast lane" means an exciting, busy, often risky lifestyle.

senses.def: the system of words and grammar used by the people of a particular country or group
examples: She speaks three languages fluently.
English is the official language of the conference.

senses.def: a particular style of speaking or writing, or words of a certain type
examples: The contract is written in very technical language.
Watch your language — there are children here.

senses.def: the flat area formed by the top of your legs when you sit down
examples: The cat jumped onto my lap and fell asleep.
She sat with her hands folded in her lap.

senses.def: one trip around a track or one length of a swimming pool
examples: He swims thirty laps every morning before work.
The leader crashed on the final lap.

note: "Fall into your lap" means to get something good without effort.

senses.def: a small computer that runs on a battery and is easy to carry
examples: I always bring my laptop when I work from a café.
The battery on my old laptop only lasts an hour.

note: "Desktop" is the non-portable kind.

senses.def: big in size, amount or number
examples: They live in a large house with a big backyard.
A large number of people attended the protest.

note: Trap: "large" means big, not "wide" (= geniş in width). "At large" = not yet caught; "by and large" = generally.

senses.def: involving many people or things, or happening over a wide area
examples: The government launched a large-scale vaccination program.
Large-scale protests broke out across the country.

note: Opposite: small-scale. Used before a noun.

senses.def: to a great degree; mostly
examples: The success of the project was largely due to her hard work.
The town's economy is largely based on tourism.

senses.def: a device that produces a strong, narrow beam of light used for cutting, surgery, etc.
examples: The surgeon used a laser to correct her eyesight.
The factory uses lasers to cut sheets of metal.

note: "Laser-focused" means extremely concentrated on one goal.

senses.def: coming after all others; final
examples: We caught the last train home.
She was the last person to leave the office.

senses.def: most recent; the one before the present one
examples: I saw him last week at the gym.
Last night's game went into overtime.

senses.def: to continue for a particular length of time, or to stay in good condition
examples: The meeting lasted three hours.
These batteries last much longer than cheap ones.

senses.def: after everything or everyone else, or most recently
examples: Our team finished last in the league.
When did you last see your wallet?

note: No "the" before time words: "last week", not "the last week" (which means "the past seven days").

senses.def: arriving or happening after the expected or usual time
examples: Sorry I'm late — the traffic was terrible.
The train was twenty minutes late.

senses.def: near the end of a period of time
examples: The house was built in the late 1800s.
She's in her late thirties.

senses.def: after the expected or usual time, or near the end of a period
examples: He stayed up late watching movies.
The package arrived two days late.

senses.def: used about someone who has died, especially recently
examples: The award was named after her late husband.

note: The adverb is "late", not "lately": "I arrived late". "Lately" means "recently".

senses.def: recently; during the period just before now
examples: Have you talked to Mark lately?
I've been feeling really tired lately.

note: Usually with the present perfect: "I haven't seen her lately." It does not mean "late".

senses.def: at a time in the future, or after the time you are talking about
examples: I'll call you back later tonight.
Two years later, they got married.

senses.def: coming after something else, or happening in the future
examples: The issue will be discussed at a later date.
In later life, she became a painter.

note: Don't confuse with "latter" (/ˈlætər/), which means the second of two things mentioned.

senses.def: the most recent or newest
examples: Have you seen the latest episode of the show?
The latest figures show unemployment is falling.

senses.tr: en son haber, en son çıkan şey
senses.def: the newest thing, fashion or piece of news
examples: This phone is the latest in smartphone technology.
Stay tuned for the latest on the storm.

note: "At the latest" sets a deadline: "Send it by Friday at the latest."

senses.def: the second of two people or things just mentioned
examples: Given the choice of tea or coffee, most people chose the latter.
Of the two plans, the latter seems more realistic.

senses.def: near the end of a period of time
examples: The company grew quickly in the latter half of the decade.

note: Opposite: "the former" (the first of two). Formal; always used with "the".

senses.def: to make sounds and move your face in a way that shows you think something is funny
examples: Everyone laughed at his joke about the boss.
We laughed until we cried.

senses.def: to show that you think someone or something is silly or not serious
examples: The other kids laughed at him because of his accent.

senses.def: the sound you make when you think something is funny
examples: She has a loud, warm laugh.
The comedian got a big laugh from the audience.

note: "Laugh at" can mean mocking. The gh is pronounced /f/.

senses.def: the act or sound of laughing
examples: The room was full of laughter during the wedding speech.
The audience burst into laughter.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of laughter", not "laughters".

senses.def: to start a planned activity, especially a large or important one
examples: Police have launched an investigation into the fire.
The charity launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.

senses.def: to make a new product available to the public
examples: The company will launch its new phone in September.

senses.def: to send a rocket or missile into the air or a boat into the water
examples: The rocket was launched from Florida early this morning.

senses.def: the act of starting or introducing something, or of sending a rocket into space
examples: The product launch was streamed live online.
The launch was delayed because of bad weather.

senses.def: an official rule made by a government that everyone must obey
examples: There's a law against texting while driving in most states.
Congress passed a new law on data privacy.

senses.def: the whole system of rules in a country, or the subject of study about them
examples: She studied law at Harvard.
Everyone is equal under the law.

senses.def: a statement describing what always happens in science or nature
examples: The law of gravity explains why objects fall.

senses.def: an area of short, cut grass, especially in front of or behind a house
examples: He mows the lawn every Saturday morning.
The kids were playing on the front lawn.

senses.def: a claim that a person or organization brings to a court of law against another
examples: The family filed a lawsuit against the hospital.
The company settled the lawsuit out of court.

note: Common verb pair: file a lawsuit (= dava açmak). You can also "sue" someone.

senses.def: a person trained to advise people about the law and represent them in court
examples: You should talk to a lawyer before signing that contract.
Her lawyer said she would appeal the decision.

note: In American English, "attorney" is common and more formal.

senses.def: to put someone or something down carefully in a flat position
examples: She laid the baby gently in the crib.
Lay the map on the table so we can all see it.

senses.def: to produce eggs
examples: Our chickens lay about six eggs a day.

senses.def: to prepare or establish something, especially the basis for later development
examples: These early studies helped lay the foundation for modern medicine.

note: Lay – laid – laid needs an object (lay the book down). Lie – lay – lain has no object (lie on the bed). "Lay off" = fire workers.

senses.def: a quantity or sheet of something that lies over a surface or between surfaces
examples: A thin layer of dust covered the furniture.
Wear several layers of clothing when you go hiking in winter.

senses.def: a level or part within a system or set of ideas
examples: Each new layer of bureaucracy slowed the project down.

senses.def: the way the parts of something, such as a page, room or building, are arranged
examples: We changed the layout of the kitchen to make more space.
The website has a clean, simple layout.

note: Noun is one word (layout); the phrasal verb is two words (lay out the plans).

senses.def: not willing to work or make an effort
examples: He's too lazy to cook, so he orders takeout every night.
The teacher said the essay was lazy and poorly researched.

senses.def: relaxed and without much activity
examples: We spent a lazy Sunday afternoon in the park.
